Application Identifier (AID)
Uniquely identifies the payment application on the card. Used by the terminal to select the correct application for processing the transaction.
Identifies which payment application to use (Visa, Mastercard, etc.). The terminal uses this to know how to communicate with the card.
Binary, typically 5-16 bytes. Registered with ISO and managed by payment networks.
Returned by the card in response to SELECT PPSE or SELECT AID commands.
Application Label
Human-readable name of the payment application. Displayed to merchants and cardholders to identify the card brand.
Provides a user-friendly name for the application, such as VISA DEBIT or MASTERCARD.
ASCII text, maximum 16 characters.
Stored on the card and returned during application selection.
Track 2 Equivalent Data
Contains the same data that would be on the magnetic stripe Track 2. Includes PAN, expiration date, and service code in a compact format.
Provides backwards compatibility with magnetic stripe systems while maintaining EMV security.
BCD encoded, up to 19 bytes. Format: PAN, separator (D), expiration (YYMM), service code, discretionary data.
Read from card records after GPO command execution.
Primary Account Number (PAN)
The card number used to identify the account. This is the main identifier for routing transactions to the correct issuer.
Uniquely identifies the cardholder account. Used for authorization and settlement of transactions.
BCD compressed, 13-19 digits. Includes issuer identification number and account number.
Retrieved from card records during transaction processing.
Cardholder Name
Name of the individual or organization to whom the card was issued. Used for verification and receipts.
Identifies the authorized cardholder. Can be displayed on receipts and used for manual verification.
ASCII text, 2-26 characters. Format: LASTNAME/FIRSTNAME or organization name.
Stored on card and read from application records.
Application Expiration Date
Date after which the application on the card is no longer valid for transactions.
Determines if the card is still valid. Terminal rejects transactions if current date exceeds this value.
BCD encoded, 3 bytes in format YYMMDD.
Read from card application data.
Application Effective Date
Date from which the application on the card becomes valid for use.
Prevents use of the card before it becomes active. Terminal checks that current date is after this value.
BCD encoded, 3 bytes in format YYMMDD.
Stored in card application data.
Issuer Country Code
Identifies the country of the institution that issued the card using ISO 3166-1 numeric code.
Used for country-specific processing rules, fraud detection, and compliance with regional regulations.
Numeric, 3 digits according to ISO 3166-1 standard.
Configured by issuer and stored on card.
Transaction Currency Code
Indicates the currency in which the transaction amount is expressed using ISO 4217 code.
Ensures both terminal and card agree on transaction currency. Critical for international transactions and currency conversion.
Numeric, 2 bytes. ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 0840 for USD, 0978 for EUR).
Sent by terminal to card, or read from card for offline transactions.
Language Preference
Indicates the cardholder preferred language for terminal display and receipt printing.
Allows terminals to display messages in the cardholder preferred language when available.
ASCII, 2-8 characters. ISO 639 language codes (e.g., en, es, fr).
Stored on card based on cardholder preference during personalization.
Service Code
Defines the services and restrictions applicable to the card, inherited from magnetic stripe specifications.
Indicates card usage restrictions, PIN requirements, and authorization methods.
Numeric, 3 digits. Each digit position has specific meaning for card capabilities.
Retrieved from card data, usually part of Track 2 data.
PAN Sequence Number
Distinguishes between separate cards with the same PAN, such as when a replacement card is issued.
Allows multiple physical cards to exist with the same account number while being uniquely identifiable.
Numeric, 1 byte. Values from 00 to 99.
Assigned by issuer during card personalization.
Application Interchange Profile (AIP)
Indicates the capabilities of the card application, including supported authentication methods and processing options.
Informs terminal which security features the card supports (SDA, DDA, CDA) and what processing is available.
Binary, 2 bytes. Each bit represents a specific capability or feature.
Returned by card in response to GET PROCESSING OPTIONS command.
Dedicated File (DF) Name
The name of the Dedicated File that represents the payment application. Typically same as AID.
Used in file selection commands to access the specific payment application on the card.
Binary, 5-16 bytes. Usually identical to the Application Identifier.
Returned during application selection process.
Application Priority Indicator
Indicates the priority of this application among multiple applications on the card for automatic selection.
Helps terminal decide which application to select when card has multiple payment applications.
Binary, 1 byte. Lower values indicate higher priority.
Defined by issuer and stored in PPSE response.
Card Risk Management Data Object List 1
List of data objects required by card for risk management in the first GENERATE AC command.
Tells terminal what data to provide when requesting the first application cryptogram for transaction authorization.
Binary DOL (Data Object List) format. Lists tags and lengths of required data.
Retrieved from card during application initialization.
Card Risk Management Data Object List 2
List of data objects required by card for risk management in the second GENERATE AC command.
Specifies data needed for second cryptogram generation, typically used for transaction completion or clearing.
Binary DOL format. May differ from CDOL1 based on transaction flow.
Retrieved from card application data.
Cardholder Verification Method List
Prioritized list of methods the card supports for verifying the cardholder identity (PIN, signature, etc.).
Determines how cardholder verification should be performed based on transaction conditions and amount.
Binary, variable length. Contains CVM codes, conditions, and amount thresholds.
Read from card application configuration.
Certification Authority Public Key Index
Index identifying which CA public key to use for verifying the issuer public key certificate.
Enables terminal to locate the correct public key for certificate chain validation in offline authentication.
Binary, 1 byte. Index value assigned by payment scheme.
Stored on card as part of security configuration.
Issuer Public Key Certificate
Certificate containing the issuer public key, signed by the Certification Authority for offline authentication.
Allows terminal to verify authenticity of issuer public key, which is then used to verify card authenticity.
Binary, variable length depending on key size. Typically RSA certificate.
Retrieved from card during offline authentication process.
Issuer Public Key Remainder
Remaining portion of issuer public key when key is too large to fit in the certificate.
Combined with certificate to reconstruct complete issuer public key for authentication.
Binary, variable length. Appended to key recovered from certificate.
Read from card along with issuer public key certificate.
Application File Locator (AFL)
Indicates locations of application data files on the card that must be read by the terminal.
Tells terminal which files and records to read to obtain all necessary card data for transaction processing.
Binary, multiple of 4 bytes. Each entry specifies Short File Identifier, record range, and authentication records.
Returned by card in GET PROCESSING OPTIONS response.
Transaction Date
Local date when the transaction was initiated at the terminal.
Used by card for validity checking and transaction logging. Critical for offline transaction approval decisions.
Numeric, 3 bytes in format YYMMDD.
Provided by terminal and sent to card during transaction.
Transaction Type
Indicates the type of financial transaction being performed (purchase, withdrawal, refund, etc.).
Informs card of transaction nature to apply appropriate processing rules and limits.
Numeric, 1 byte. Standard values: 00 (purchase), 01 (cash), 09 (cashback), 20 (refund).
Set by terminal based on transaction context.
Amount, Authorised (Numeric)
Authorized amount of the transaction in the transaction currency, excluding cashback.
Primary transaction amount used by card for authorization decisions and limit checking.
Numeric, 6 bytes BCD. Right-justified with leading zeros, no decimal point.
Provided by terminal during transaction initialization.
Amount, Other (Numeric)
Secondary amount associated with the transaction, such as cashback amount.
Allows separate tracking of additional amounts beyond the primary purchase amount.
Numeric, 6 bytes BCD. Same format as authorized amount.
Provided by terminal when transaction includes cashback or other secondary amount.
Application Usage Control
Indicates issuer restrictions on the geographic usage and services available for the application.
Enforces restrictions like domestic-only use, ATM restrictions, or service limitations.
Binary, 2 bytes. Each bit represents a specific restriction or permission.
Configured by issuer during card personalization.
Application Version Number (Card)
Version number of the EMV application on the card, assigned by payment scheme.
Ensures compatibility between card and terminal application versions. Used for version-specific processing.
Binary, 2 bytes. Format determined by payment scheme.
Stored on card and read during application selection.
Cardholder Name Extended
Extended or alternate cardholder name that may include additional information beyond standard name field.
Provides additional name information when standard name field is insufficient.
ASCII, variable length up to 45 characters.
Optionally stored on card for extended name support.
Issuer Action Code - Default
Conditions that cause transaction to be rejected by card if online authorization is unavailable.
Defines issuer risk management policy for offline transaction decisions when terminal cannot go online.
Binary, 5 bytes. Bitmap of Terminal Verification Results conditions.
Configured by issuer and stored on card.
Issuer Action Code - Denial
Conditions that cause transaction to be denied by card regardless of online capability.
Hard limits set by issuer for unconditional transaction rejection based on risk conditions.
Binary, 5 bytes. Bitmap of Terminal Verification Results conditions.
Configured by issuer for risk management.
Issuer Action Code - Online
Conditions that cause card to request online authorization from issuer.
Determines when card requires online authorization for additional security or issuer decision.
Binary, 5 bytes. Bitmap of Terminal Verification Results conditions.
Configured by issuer based on risk policy.
Issuer Application Data
Proprietary data from issuer for use in financial processing and clearing.
Contains issuer-specific information that may be needed for authorization and settlement processing.
Binary, variable length. Format defined by issuer.
Generated by card and included in authorization request.
Application Preferred Name
Preferred mnemonic associated with the application, for display purposes.
Provides alternative display name that may be more recognizable to cardholder than standard label.
ASCII, 1-16 characters.
Configured during application personalization.
Terminal Country Code
Country code of the terminal location using ISO 3166-1 numeric format.
Used by card to determine if transaction is domestic or international, affecting authorization rules.
Numeric, 2 bytes. ISO 3166-1 country code.
Configured in terminal based on deployment location.
Transaction Time
Local time when the transaction was initiated at the terminal.
Provides precise timestamp for transaction logging and fraud detection.
Numeric, 3 bytes in format HHMMSS.
Provided by terminal from system clock.
Application Cryptogram
Cryptogram generated by card to provide evidence of transaction authorization. Can be TC, ARQC, or AAC.
Proves card authenticity and creates secure proof of transaction that cannot be forged.
Binary, 8 bytes. Cryptographic MAC computed over transaction data.
Generated by card in response to GENERATE AC command.
Cryptogram Information Data
Indicates the type of cryptogram returned by card and reasons for the card decision.
Tells terminal what type of cryptogram was generated (approval, online request, or decline) and why.
Binary, 1 byte. Contains cryptogram type and card action codes.
Returned with application cryptogram from card.
Issuer Public Key Exponent
Exponent of the issuer public key used in RSA algorithm for offline authentication.
Required component for reconstructing issuer public key to verify card authenticity.
Binary, 1 or 3 bytes. Common values are 03 or 010001.
Read from card during authentication process.
Terminal Capabilities
Indicates the card data input, CVM, and security capabilities of the terminal.
Informs card what features terminal supports so card can make appropriate processing decisions.
Binary, 3 bytes. Bitmaps for card data input methods, CVM capabilities, and security capabilities.
Configured in terminal based on hardware capabilities.
Cardholder Verification Method Results
Indicates the results of the cardholder verification performed by terminal.
Documents which CVM was performed and whether it was successful for auditing and authorization.
Binary, 3 bytes. Contains CVM performed, condition codes, and result.
Generated by terminal after CVM processing.
Terminal Type
Indicates the environment of the terminal and its operational control.
Helps card apply appropriate risk management based on terminal type (attended, unattended, online, offline).
Numeric, 1 byte. Values like 22 (attended online), 14 (unattended offline).
Configured in terminal based on deployment.
Application Transaction Counter (ATC)
Counter incremented by card for each transaction, used for replay attack prevention.
Ensures each transaction has unique counter value, making transaction data non-replayable for security.
Binary, 2 bytes. Increments with each GENERATE AC command.
Maintained by card and included in cryptogram generation.
Unpredictable Number
Random number generated by terminal to ensure uniqueness of each transaction.
Provides entropy for cryptogram generation, preventing pre-computation attacks and ensuring transaction uniqueness.
Binary, 4 bytes. Should be randomly generated for each transaction.
Generated by terminal and sent to card during processing.
Processing Options Data Object List
List of terminal data required by card for the GET PROCESSING OPTIONS command.
Tells terminal what data to provide when initializing transaction processing with the card.
Binary DOL format. Lists required data objects with their expected lengths.
Retrieved from card during application selection.
Application Currency Code
Currency code of the application according to ISO 4217.
Indicates default currency for the application, used when transaction currency differs for conversion.
Numeric, 2 bytes. ISO 4217 currency code.
Stored on card during personalization.
Application Currency Exponent
Number of decimal places for the application currency.
Defines how to interpret currency amounts (e.g., 2 for cents, 0 for non-decimal currencies).
Numeric, 1 byte. Typically 00 or 02.
Stored with application currency configuration.
Data Authentication Code
Result of authentication processing for Dynamic Data Authentication.
Provides cryptographic proof that card data has not been altered during transaction.
Binary, 2 bytes. Generated during DDA or CDA.
Generated by card as part of dynamic authentication.
ICC Public Key Certificate
Certificate containing the card (ICC) public key, signed by issuer for offline authentication.
Enables terminal to verify card public key, which is used for dynamic data authentication.
Binary, variable length. RSA certificate signed by issuer.
Read from card during DDA or CDA authentication.
ICC Public Key Exponent
Exponent of the card public key used in RSA algorithm.
Required for reconstructing card public key for dynamic authentication.
Binary, 1 or 3 bytes. Commonly 03 or 010001.
Read from card along with ICC public key certificate.
ICC Public Key Remainder
Remaining portion of card public key when too large to fit in certificate.
Combined with certificate to form complete card public key.
Binary, variable length based on key size.
Read from card during authentication.
Static Data Authentication Tag List
List of tags of data objects to be included in Static Data Authentication.
Specifies which data elements are protected by SDA signature for integrity verification.
Binary, variable length. List of tag identifiers.
Configured on card for SDA-capable applications.
ICC Dynamic Number
Time-variant number generated by card for Combined DDA/AC generation.
Provides dynamic component for CDA authentication, ensuring freshness of card response.
Binary, 2-8 bytes generated by card.
Generated by card during CDA processing.
Transaction Log Entry
Contains transaction log data maintained by card for offline transactions.
Allows issuer to retrieve transaction history from card for reconciliation and fraud detection.
Binary, variable length. Format defined by card application.
Stored on card for each completed transaction.
Form Factor Indicator
Indicates the form factor of the consumer payment device and its ability to change form factors.
Identifies if payment device is card, phone, wearable, etc. Used for appropriate transaction processing.
Binary, 4 bytes. Indicates device type and characteristics.
Stored on device during provisioning.
Merchant Custom Data
Custom data defined by merchant for inclusion in authorization request.
Allows merchant to include additional proprietary information in transaction processing.
Binary, variable length. Format defined by merchant.
Generated by terminal based on merchant requirements.
